output_text: The study will test the effects of both types of cigarettes on volunteers' blood vessel function, recruiting 135 adult smokers who have smoked 15 cigarettes a day for at least two years. Participants will be divided into three groups: one continuing to smoke tobacco cigarettes, another switching to e-cigarettes containing nicotine and flavor, and a third switching to e-cigarettes containing flavor alone. Dr. Jacob George from the university's school of medicine aims to determine whether e-cigarettes are safer for blood vessel function compared to traditional cigarettes, despite the presence of nicotine.
